subject: History
description: Covers Rowlatt Act, Satyapal/Kitchlew, Jallianwala Bagh, Tagore knighthood, Hunter Commission, and Udham Singh.

questions.stem: The Rowlatt Act of 1919, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, was passed to extend the emergency measures of the Defence of India Act 1915. What was its most draconian provision?

options.option_text: It allowed the colonial government to arrest and imprison any person without trial or judicial review for up to two years
It strictly banned all Indians from carrying firearms without a license
It imposed censorship on all vernacular newspapers published in Indian languages
It mandated the separation of electorates based on religion for provincial councils

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Rowlatt Act gave the British colonial government sweeping, dictatorial powers to suppress political dissent. The most infamous provision was the power to arrest any person suspected of "terrorist" activities and hold them in prison for up to two years WITHOUT trial, without a lawyer, and without the right to appeal (famously described as "No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal").
DECOY BUSTING: Banning firearms was the Arms Act (1878). Censorship of local press was the Vernacular Press Act (1878). Separate electorates were introduced by the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909).
EXAM INSIGHT: The passage of the Rowlatt Act sparked nationwide fury. Gandhi organized the Rowlatt Satyagraha, marking his first attempt at leading an ALL-INDIA mass strike. The peaceful protests against this act in Punjab ultimately culminated in the horrific Jallianwala Bagh massacre on April 13, 1919.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Who were the two prominent nationalist leaders arrested in Amritsar whose deportation led to the massive, peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh on April 13, 1919?

options.option_text: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal
Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were immensely popular local leaders in Punjab who were leading peaceful protests against the Rowlatt Act. On April 10, 1919, they were secretly arrested and deported by the British authorities. This sparked widespread anger. On April 13 (the day of the Baisakhi festival), thousands of people gathered at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar—partly to celebrate the festival, and partly to peacefully protest the arrest of these two leaders.
DECOY BUSTING: Lala Lajpat Rai was a major leader in Punjab but wasn't the trigger for this specific event. Bhagat Singh was a child at the time (the massacre deeply influenced him). Nehru and Das were national leaders, not the local focal points in Amritsar.
EXAM INSIGHT: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer entered the enclosed ground with his troops, blocked the only exit, and ordered his men to fire indiscriminately into the unarmed crowd without warning, killing hundreds. This brutality shattered any remaining illusions of British justice.

questions.stem: Following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which eminent Indian returned his Knighthood to the British Crown in protest, declaring that 'badges of honour make our shame glaring in the incongruous context of humiliation'?

options.option_text: Rabindranath Tagore
Mahatma Gandhi
Subhas Chandra Bose
Bal Gangadhar Tilak

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Rabindranath Tagore, the Nobel Laureate, was knighted by King George V in 1915. Horrified by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, Tagore wrote a scorching letter to the Viceroy, Lord Chelmsford, on May 31, 1919, renouncing his knighthood. He famously stated that the time has come when badges of honour make our shame glaring in the incongruous context of humiliation, and he wished to stand shorn of all special distinctions with his countrymen.
DECOY BUSTING: Mahatma Gandhi returned his 'Kaiser-i-Hind' gold medal (awarded for his ambulance work in the Boer War), but he was never knighted. Bose resigned from the ICS later. 
EXAM INSIGHT: Questions about who surrendered which title/medal in response to Jallianwala Bagh are classic UPSC/State PSC traps. Tagore = Knighthood; Gandhi = Kaiser-i-Hind.

questions.stem: The British Government appointed a commission to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre due to mounting public pressure. What was the name of this commission?

options.option_text: Hunter Commission
Simon Commission
Cabinet Mission
Cripps Mission

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Disorders Inquiry Committee, widely known as the Hunter Commission (after its chairman, Lord William Hunter), was established in October 1919 to investigate the disturbances in Punjab, including the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Simon Commission (1927) was sent to review constitutional reforms (met with 'Simon Go Back' protests). The Cripps Mission (1942) tried to secure Indian cooperation in WWII. The Cabinet Mission (1946) discussed the transfer of power.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Hunter Commission condemned General Dyer's actions but did not impose any penal or disciplinary action; he was merely relieved of his command and allowed to retire on half-pay. The Indian National Congress, dissatisfied with this whitewash, appointed its own unofficial committee (including Gandhi, Motilal Nehru, and C.R. Das) to investigate the truth.

questions.stem: Who assassinated Michael O'Dwyer, the former Lieutenant Governor of Punjab who had endorsed General Dyer's actions at Jallianwala Bagh, in London in 1940?

options.option_text: Udham Singh
Bhagat Singh
Chandrashekhar Azad
Madan Lal Dhingra

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Sardar Udham Singh, an Indian revolutionary associated with the Ghadar Party, assassinated Sir Michael O'Dwyer on March 13, 1940, at Caxton Hall in London. O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab during the 1919 massacre and had publicly supported Brigadier-General Dyer's brutal actions. Udham Singh waited 21 years to take his revenge.
DECOY BUSTING: Bhagat Singh assassinated John Saunders in Lahore (1928) to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909. 
EXAM INSIGHT: It is crucial to distinguish between the two 'Dyers'. Brigadier-General REGINALD Dyer was the military officer who actually ordered the troops to fire. He died of a stroke in 1927. Sir MICHAEL O'Dwyer was the civilian Governor of the province who backed him. Udham Singh killed O'Dwyer, not Reginald Dyer.

questions.stem: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of April 13, 1919 coincided with a major annual gathering for which festival, explaining why thousands were assembled in the enclosed garden?

options.option_text: Baisakhi, the Punjabi harvest and new year festival
Diwali, the pan-Indian festival of lights in October
Holi, the spring festival of colours celebrated in March
Guru Nanak Jayanti, the Sikh founder's birth anniversary

questions.explanation: Baisakhi (April 13) is the Punjabi new year and harvest festival; the Bagh was crowded precisely because people had gathered for both the festival and a public meeting. Guru Nanak Jayanti is tempting because the event is Sikh-connected, but it falls in October–November, not April.

questions.stem: To organise civil resistance against the Rowlatt Act, Gandhi established which body in February 1919 in Bombay, whose members took a formal pledge to defy the legislation?

options.option_text: Indian Home Rule League, founded by Annie Besant in 1916
Ghadar Party, a revolutionary overseas Indian movement
Satyagraha Sabha, a pledge-based civil-resistance body
Hindustani Seva Dal, a Congress volunteer service corps

questions.explanation: Gandhi established the Satyagraha Sabha in Bombay in February 1919; signatories pledged to defy the Rowlatt Act and court arrest. The Home Rule League (Option A) pre-dated this and was Besant's/Tilak's separate formation; the Ghadar Party was a violent revolutionary overseas body, not Gandhi's instrument.

questions.stem: The Rowlatt Act specified that offences listed in its schedule would be tried by a special court with a distinctive composition. What was that composition and its key procedural restriction?

options.option_text: Five judges drawn from the Federal Court of India only
Three High Court judges, with no right of appeal to any court
A single district judge appointed by the Provincial Governor
Two judges and one military officer as a joint civil-military tribunal

questions.explanation: The Act provided for a special court of three High Court judges; crucially, its decisions were final with no right of appeal — one prong of the nationalist slogan 'no vakil, no daleel, no appeal'. The Federal Court (Option A) was not established until 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.stem: Which Viceroy of India was in office when both the Rowlatt Act was passed and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred, and who later received the Hunter Commission's report?

options.option_text: Lord Irwin, who later negotiated the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931)
Lord Curzon, who had partitioned Bengal in 1905 controversially
Lord Reading, who succeeded as Viceroy and imprisoned Gandhi in 1922
Lord Chelmsford, who served as Viceroy from 1916 to 1921

questions.explanation: Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy 1916–1921) presided over both the passage of the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; the Hunter Commission reported to him and Secretary of State Edwin Montagu. Lord Irwin is the most common confusion, as he is the Viceroy associated with Gandhi's civil disobedience era a decade later.

questions.stem: After violence broke out in several cities during the Rowlatt Satyagraha of April 1919, Gandhi suspended the campaign. In what phrase did he publicly describe his own error in misjudging popular readiness for non-violent mass action?

options.option_text: Himalayan miscalculation, a grave error of personal judgement
Moral bankruptcy and total failure of nationalist leadership
Strategic retreat to consolidate national consciousness first
Necessary sacrifice to shield innocent civilian lives then

questions.explanation: Gandhi used the phrase 'Himalayan miscalculation' to admit that he had gravely erred in launching mass civil disobedience before the populace was disciplined enough to remain non-violent. Option C ('strategic retreat') is wrong because Gandhi explicitly framed it as a blunder, not a calculated withdrawal.

questions.stem: After the Hunter Commission censured General Dyer, a section of British imperialist opinion mounted a public subscription drive that raised approximately £26,000 in his honour. Which London newspaper spearheaded this fund?

options.option_text: The Times of London, the oldest and most influential broadsheet
The Morning Post, a Conservative paper supportive of empire
The Daily Telegraph, which had reported extensively on Punjab
The Manchester Guardian, edited by C. P. Scott at that time

questions.explanation: The Morning Post, a right-wing Conservative newspaper, ran the 'Morning Post Dyer Fund' subscription in 1920, lionising Dyer as a saviour of empire. The Times took a more neutral line; The Manchester Guardian, under the liberal C. P. Scott, was sympathetic to Indian grievances and would not have championed Dyer.

questions.stem: Nationalist leaders condensed their objection to the Rowlatt Act's special court procedure in the slogan 'no vakil, no daleel, no appeal'. What did the phrase 'no daleel' specifically signify as a procedural deprivation?

options.option_text: No right to cross-examine witnesses produced by the prosecution
No right to know the evidence or exact charges framed against oneself
No right to argue or place a defence plea before the special court
No right to seek transfer of the case to a regular High Court bench

questions.explanation: 'Daleel' (Urdu/Hindi) means argument or plea; 'no daleel' meant the accused could not argue or present a defence before the special court. 'No vakil' meant no legal counsel, and 'no appeal' meant no higher-court review. Option B (no right to know charges) is a related grievance but is captured separately by the secrecy-of-evidence clause, not the term 'daleel'.
